title: dedicated-autoscaler: token-bucket burst controller + utilization reporting improvements
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: Customers with Dedicated fleets have asked for predictable throughput guarantees while still allowing short-term bursts for traffic spikes. The existing autoscaler allowed uncontrolled bursts that caused noisy multi-tenant interference and inaccurate billing. This PR introduces a token-bucket-based burst controller integrated into the Dedicated fleet autoscaler, improves utilization reporting to include per-fleet burst_budget and burst_usage metrics, and adds conservative admission controls to ensure throughput guarantees are respected. Changes include: 1) token_bucket_controller: core implementation and config schema for burst_capacity, refill_rate, and max_burst_duration; 2) autoscaler hook: admission logic that checks burst budget and fallbacks to queued requests or lower-tier model variants; 3) metrics exporter: per-fleet metrics (dedicated.fleet.burst_budget, dedicated.fleet.burst_used, dedicated.fleet.utilization_5m) and tags for customer_id and region; 4) console integration: warnings in fleet view when burst_budget below threshold and a new chart for burst usage; 5) CLI/config: two new flags and a migration script to backfill historical utilization; 6) tests: unit tests, integration tests in perf-canary, and a canary rollout plan.; Context: This is the second iteration after customer-facing incidents in Jan 2026 where bursts exhausted shared spare capacity. The design balances SLO guarantees with practical burst allowances. Related: ENG-4621 (throughput guarantees), ENG-4712 (billing accuracy). Rollout plan: feature flag gated, canary on small fleets for 48h with rollback conditions tied to latency SLO and burst_budget depletion. Breaking change: false.
